Until now
column2: destroying a protected guest was an entirely synchronous

column1: operation that could potentially take a very long time
the size of the guest
column2: due to the time needed to clean up the address

column1: space from protected pages.
This patch implements an asynchronous destroy mechanism
protected guest to reboot significantly faster than previously.
This is achieved by clearing the pages of the old guest in background.
In case of reboot
column2: the new guest will be able to run in the same

column1: address space almost immediately.
The old protected guest is then only destroyed when all of its memory
has been destroyed or otherwise made non protected.
Two new PV commands are added for the KVM_S390_PV_COMMAND ioctl:
KVM_PV_ASYNC_CLEANUP_PREPARE: set aside the current protected VM for
later asynchronous teardown. The current KVM VM will then continue
immediately as non-protected. If a protected VM had already been
set aside for asynchronous teardown
process
column2: this call will fail. There can be at most one VM set aside at

column1: any time. Once it is set aside
column2: the protected VM only exists in the

column1: context of the Ultravisor
column2: it is not associated with the KVM VM

column1: anymore. Its protected CPUs have already been destroyed
memory. This command can be issued again immediately after starting
KVM_PV_ASYNC_CLEANUP_PERFORM
column2: without having to wait for completion.

column1: KVM_PV_ASYNC_CLEANUP_PERFORM: tears down the protected VM previously
set aside using KVM_PV_ASYNC_CLEANUP_PREPARE. Ideally the
KVM_PV_ASYNC_CLEANUP_PERFORM PV command should be issued by userspace
from a separate thread. If a fatal signal is received (or if the
process terminates naturally)
without completing. All protected VMs whose teardown was interrupted
will be put in the need_cleanup list. The rest of the normal KVM
teardown process will take care of properly cleaning up all remaining
protected VMs
column2: including the ones on the need_cleanup list.
